content: Hi, I recently closed the last few goals in a Lean proof of the yoneda lemma for bicategories. It still could use a bit of golfing and clean up. I should also disclose I did use AI for parts of the formalization. I think this would be a good addition to mathlib as right now it has the bicategorical yoneda embedding but not the lemma. I would like to start making some PRs with some of the lemmas and constructions I have done and eventually get the whole thing in mathlib. My repository for this project is https://github.com/SpencerWoolfson/biyoneda. Dose this seem like a good plan and is there anything I should know?

I had only a quick look at the repo and it seems there are at least a few things to change:

  • I see that you defined the evaluation pseudofunctor as a pseudofunctor out of a product bicategory. In Mathlib in general, we tend to prefer the curried versions (i.e., pseudofunctors to categories of pseudofunctors) over the ones out of products.
  • The final definition in your repository is a BiEquiv, i.e. a non-adjoint equivalence. Equivalences internal to bicategories in Mathlib are adjoint equivalences, and we basically only work with those. You should drop the BiEquiv entirely and construct a Bicategory.Equivalence. (I didn’t think about this very much, but I would be very surprised if you can’t make the equivalence for the Yoneda equivalence an adjoint equivalence).
  • Overall, the code seems to be very far from the quality expected in mathlib: for instance the proof of forwards_naturality_comp_core in the file Biyoneda/Forwards.lean is way too long. You should read the existing code in Mathlib’s directory on bicategory to see what the typical code about bicategories looks like.

Thank you for taking a look. I tried to match the one-yoneda lemma which uses the products. I can change it to define the un-curried versions first and construct them via curring. Biequiv should be the same thing as adjoint equivalences so that will be an easy fix. I will also dedicate some real effort to golf these proofs.
